findings.message: docs/economy-online-coverage.md row 32 (MatchRoom.stepShop, 'A bought id is kept for good') is marked `equivalent`, but the reason given is wrong. If the room evicted a bought tonic id along with its refusals, a retry would not reach the ledger's replay first. It would be queued, and stepShop runs the room's own `not-at-dock` check before `purchase`, so a retry sent at sea would get a new `not-at-dock` refusal instead of the replayed `bought` answer. Deleting the branch therefore changes what a player sees. The row should be `tested`, with a test that retries a bought id at sea after 16 later refusals; the existing retry-after-16-refusals test covers only drinks. The code itself is correct: bought ids are kept forever.
findings.requirement: A branch that can't change the outcome is marked `equivalent`, with a one-line reason.

findings.message: The hold diagnostics count any held interact/fruit button, not only real holds. In InputGate.worldStepTaken/receive, a player sailing at sea with E held who hits a stall counts as `gapsBridged`, as holds.test.ts 'keeps movement's 250 ms lapse' itself shows. A dropped connection with E held logs a 'held hold button lapsed' warning and increments `holdsLapsed` even when no collection, cache claim, meal or treasure claim was in progress. The counters therefore overstate hold gaps and lapses in the room's diagnostics. Gating the counting and the log on an active channel (a ledger channel, a fruit channel or the claim) would make them measure what the operator's bug is about.
findings.requirement: per-player room counters (gaps bridged, holds lapsed) appear in the room's diagnostics, and a lapse after the grace window is logged.

findings.message: Acceptance item 3 says a ship at full speed 'moves 43 sub-units per tick then' for the steps of ticks t+1 to t+240. Because of the tuning's acceleration of 3, the implementation and tests (economy.test.ts and simulation.test.ts) move 42 on t+1 and 43 on t+2 through t+240. The cap is 43 on every one of those steps, as the design requires, and the worker disclosed this reading in open_assumptions. Noted so the operator knows the literal 'moves 43' starts one tick later; no code change is needed if this reading is accepted.
findings.requirement: A ship at full speed on a cardinal heading moves 43 sub-units per tick then, and 39 again from tick t+241 (the speed is clamped that tick), measured on the server.

findings.message: No test asserts 43 sub-units on tick t+1. Both the integration test (tests/integration/economy.test.ts, 'drunk on tick t, sails the steps of ticks t+1 to t+240 at a 43 cap', expect(moves.get(t + 1)).toBe(42)) and the unit test (packages/simulation/src/simulation.test.ts, 'lifts the cap to 43 ...', expect(moves[0]).toBe(39 + acceleration)) pin 42 on tick t+1 and 43 only from t+2 to t+240. That fits the 'cap' reading, and the worker disclosed it as an open assumption. It departs from the acceptance's literal 43 a tick for the steps of t+1 through t+240, so the tests lock in the acceleration reading. The operator should confirm that reading. The clamp to 39 from t+241 and the diagonal rounding are asserted.
findings.requirement: A ship at full speed on a cardinal heading moves 43 sub-units per tick then, and 39 again from tick t+241 (the speed is clamped that tick), measured on the server.

findings.message: The disconnected refusal of a tonic purchase (and of a drink) has no server-side test. apps/server/src/shop.test.ts maps insufficient-gold, tonic-limit and player-in-duel through tonicPurchaseOf, but never a ledger player marked disconnected. No integration test queues a buy-tonic or use-tonic and disconnects the player before the processing tick. If 'player-disconnected' were dropped from PURCHASE_REFUSALS or USE_REFUSALS in apps/server/src/shop.ts, the mapper would throw and fault the world tick, and no test would fail. Only the web text for the refusal is covered (apps/web/src/shop.test.ts).
findings.requirement: Refusals (`insufficient-gold`, `tonic-limit`, in a duel, disconnected, not at a dock) are shown and cost nothing.

findings.message: Row 89 of docs/economy-online-coverage.md (config.ts topSpeed, 'The bonus only while boosted', deletion S6) gives only 'packages/simulation/src/simulation.test.ts' in the test column. It doesn't name the test that fails when the branch is deleted, as every other tested row does.
findings.requirement: the file and function, the branch, and the test that fails when the branch is deleted.
